chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Stride pianists and the cutting contests at Monroe's
summary: Cheatham loved the piano cutting contests of James P., Willie the Lion and Fats Waller, won partly by comedy, held at Monroe's.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now New York was something special, wasn't it, I mean there was a lot of -- there was -- for instance, you know James P. Johnson played a lot down at Cafe Society --
Uh-huh, yes.
And there was that stride piano, you hadn't had any of that in Chicago, had you?
That's right, no they didn't have any of that in Chicago. No.
Uh-huh.

And that was a very interesting experience, because I liked those piano cutting contests that they were having. Around here. Wow, they took my mind off everything else because I thought that was a great thing.
Who did you hear at these cutting contests?
I heard all of them. I heard James P., and Willie the Lion Smith, and Fats Waller.
Uh-huh.
And there were a few others, but I don't think they were well known at that time.
So did the audience reaction determine who won the contest?
Well, yes, I think a little comedy had a lot to do with it, too. Fats, you know, he was like a comedian, also, you know.
Uh-huh
And then there was Willie the Lion with his hat and cigar, he'd tell Fats, get up from there, you know, and that was what the people, really mostly knocked

more so by that, than then what they were playing, because they all played, you can't get away from that, they all played, but I mean it was the comedy part of it that was funny, when the cat walked it they say, get off here, who is that down there. Get off there, you know all that, then they'd just started playing and the drinks was flying and the place, you know, would be in an uproar over that sort of thing. I think all the guys were playing.
Now these cutting contests took place in places like the Cafe Society, did they?
No, Places like, when I first round the place, up on Lennox Avenue, Barrons, or some kind of place like that, Barron's, I think was the name of the place on Nest Club Glove, or something like that --
Yeah. There was also a place called Monroe's.
Monroe's oh, that's the name I was thinking about, that's where they took place.
Uh-huh, right. And the Hee-Haw?
Well, the Hee-Haw, nevermew too much about the Hee-Haw. But Monroe's that was the place where you could bet you go there and going to have some kind of cutting contest there.
